clue.text: One handing out punishment is more decent going round island

indicators.note: going round means wrapping about something, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: chaste means pure or decent; this is its comparative
IS is the standard abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A disciplinarian is described as morally upright while travelling around an island.
explanation.definitionFit: To chastise is to punish or rebuke, so a chastiser is the person who metes out that punishment.

clue.text: Amusing play without denouement pertaining to oneself is a a source of disappointment

indicators.note: a denouement is the ending, so going without it means losing the final letter

parts.note: a comedy is an amusing play
your own things belong to yourself

explanation.surface: A comic play with no proper ending, about its own author, lets the audience down.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue repeats 'a' ('is a a source'); the duplicate is a typo and plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedown is a fall in status or an anticlimax, something that disappoints.

clue.text: A model upset fabulist

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: to model is to pose

explanation.surface: A model is upset by a teller of tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop is the ancient Greek storyteller famed for his fables, the archetypal fabulist.

clue.text: Novel arrangement of undersea trials?

indicators.note: an arrangement puts the letters into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A new way of organising tests carried out beneath the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Novel looks like an adjective meaning new, but it is the noun: Stevenson's pirate story, apt for a sea-themed surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure Island is Robert Louis Stevenson's 1883 adventure novel about pirates and buried gold.

clue.text: Cunning saint brewed ale at primarily teetotal house

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint

indicators.note: brewed suggests mixing and fermenting, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of teetotal
H is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A crafty holy man makes beer in a house where nobody drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealth is secret, sly action, so as a noun it matches cunning in the sense of craftiness.

clue.text: Starts again with amount of money secured by fortune-teller from the east

indicators.note: secured by means held fast by, so one piece is gripped inside another
reading from the east means right to left, so the word is turned around

parts.note: a seer foretells the future
a sum is an amount of money

explanation.surface: A clairvoyant takes cash and gets back to work.
explanation.definitionFit: To resume is to begin again after a pause, matching the third-person verb form.

clue.text: To start with, try on girlfriend's sexy clothes!

indicators.note: to start with points at the opening letter of each word that follows

parts.note: the initial letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Someone suggests trying on the girlfriend's racy outfit, starting there.
explanation.definitionFit: Togs is an informal British word for clothes, especially sports kit or swimwear.

clue.text: Players with gold casket presented to ancient sun god

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold
a chest is a casket or box
Ra was the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: Musicians offer a golden box to an Egyptian deity.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a body of instrumental musicians, that is, players.

clue.text: Day during which police officer, head of surveillance, finds one gratified by inflicting pain on others

definitions.text: one gratified by inflicting pain on others

indicators.note: during which means within that span, so the following pieces go inside

parts.note: SAT is short for Saturday
DI is a detective inspector

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of surveillance

explanation.surface: On a day of surveillance, a detective uncovers a cruel person.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadist takes pleasure in causing suffering to other people.

clue.text: Ordinary places where grass might grow

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an idiom for everyday or unremarkable

definitions.note: read literally: a common, or a garden
definitions.meaning: second meaning: read literally, a village green or a back lawn

explanation.walkthrough: A common is a patch of open public grassland in British villages; read word for word, the phrase names two grassy spots.
explanation.definitionFit: Common-or-garden is a British idiom for something ordinary, everyday, nothing special.

clue.text: Author Kate taking supermodel to Europe

parts.note: Kate Moss, the famous supermodel
E is the abbreviation for Europe

explanation.surface: A writer called Kate brings a fashion model across to Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter plays on two famous Kates: the model Moss supplies the start of the novelist Kate Mosse, author of Labyrinth.
explanation.definitionFit: Kate Mosse is a British novelist, best known for the historical thriller Labyrinth.

clue.text: Settled comfortably in newly built den, consuming calorie-laden cake

indicators.note: consuming means taking something inside, so one part is swallowed by another
laden means loaded with something, so the following word carries a letter inside it
something newly built has been put together afresh, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a scone is a small plain cake
C is the abbreviation for calorie

explanation.surface: Someone has made themselves at home in a new den, eating fattening cake.
explanation.walkthrough: There are two insertions, one inside the other: the calorie goes into the cake first, and that whole cake then goes into the rebuilt den.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ensconced is to have settled oneself snugly and securely in a place.

clue.text: Corrupt, so plead for removal from high office

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or perverted from its proper form, so the letters are twisted

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A crooked official begs not to be thrown out of a top job.
explanation.definitionFit: Deposal is the act of deposing a ruler, ousting someone from power.

clue.text: Fellows getting close to harem by remains of fire

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of harem
embers are the glowing remnants of a fire

explanation.surface: Men gather near a harem beside a dying fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Fellows of a society or college are its members, so the plural nouns match.

clue.text: Ruin tuna stew and retch, serving vegetable!

indicators.note: to ruin is to wreck, so the letters are smashed and rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook spoils a fish stew, gags at it, and serves up a vegetable instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The water chestnut is the crunchy edible corm of an aquatic sedge, used as a vegetable in Chinese cooking.

clue.text: Reprimanded and marked as having been done

definitions.meaning: second meaning: checked off a list

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are past participles, so each swaps neatly for the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticked off is informal for scolded, and literally describes items given a tick on a list once completed.

clue.text: Worried by puddings rising

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means going upward, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: puddings are desserts in British usage

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious about desserts that won't rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Stressed means under strain and anxious, so it is a synonym for worried.

clue.text: Hectic bankers jostled over a piece of meat

indicators.note: jostled means pushed about roughly, so the letters are shoved into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Harried bankers jostle each other in a lunch queue over a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A chicken breast is a single cut of poultry, so it is one piece of meat.

clue.text: Place to keep dogs heartens heartbroken Nelson

indicators.note: heartens is read as 'puts at the heart', so the answer sits inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A heartbroken Nelson is cheered up by a place to keep dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: Heartens looks like a verb meaning cheers, but it is the signal that the answer lies within heartbroKEN NELSon.
explanation.definitionFit: Kennels is a boarding establishment where dogs are housed and cared for.

clue.text: Close thing used to fasten garment

parts.note: nigh means near or close
a tie is something that binds or fastens

explanation.surface: A garment's fastener is close at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightie is a nightdress, a garment worn in bed.

clue.text: Scared stiff by a disfigured hag with serpent's extremities

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: disfigured means spoiled in shape, so the letters are deformed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: extremities are the far ends, so only the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of serpent

explanation.surface: Someone is terrified by an ugly old woman with snakes, like Medusa.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast means filled with horror or shock, much the same as scared stiff.

clue.text: German replacing head of KGB in Russian government structure is a source of trouble

indicators.note: replacing means taking the place of, so one letter is swapped out for another

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for German

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the letter that is swapped out
the Kremlin is the Moscow citadel housing the Russian government

explanation.surface: A German agent takes over from the KGB chief inside the Kremlin and causes trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A gremlin is an imaginary mischievous sprite blamed for unexplained faults, hence any cause of trouble.

clue.text: Hook used to secure good, rare fruit

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
R is an abbreviation for rare
an apple is a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone uses a hook to get hold of some fine, unusual fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A grapple is a grappling iron, a hooked instrument for seizing and holding something fast.

clue.text: Deposit on a coat

parts.note: to park is to put down or deposit
taken as written

explanation.surface: Paying a deposit on a coat in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, on means placed above, so the first piece sits over the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A parka is a hooded windproof coat.

clue.text: Decoration of alternative road taken by chaps in books

indicators.note: an alternative version of a word is a different arrangement of its letters

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible
chaps are men

explanation.surface: A bookish picture of fellows wandering down a different road, as an ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords, books usually means the New Testament (or OT, the Old); here the chaps are placed inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An adornment is something added to beautify, which is what a decoration is.

clue.text: Rushes game

definitions.meaning: first meaning: moves suddenly and swiftly
second meaning: the pub game played by throwing at a board

explanation.walkthrough: Rushes looks like a noun (the plants), but it is a verb, and the pub game is the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: To dart is to move with sudden speed, and the throwing game played at a dartboard shares the spelling.

clue.text: Drugs scored from sweet member of the upper classes

indicators.note: scored from means struck out of, so letters are crossed off the word that follows

parts.note: toffee is a chewy sweet
E is slang for ecstasy, so two doses are drugs

explanation.surface: A posh person who scored drugs is caught out over a sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: Scored looks like slang for buying drugs, but it means crossed out: both Es leave TOFFEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Toff is British slang for a rich or aristocratic person, a member of the upper classes.

clue.text: Official welcoming in sailors going ahead? On the contrary

indicators.note: welcoming in means letting a guest inside, so one piece is held within the other

parts.note: a steward is an official who manages events or races
RN is the Royal Navy, a body of sailors

explanation.surface: An official lets some sailors aboard who are going forward, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the opposite of going ahead: moving toward the back of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Sternward means towards the stern, the rear of a vessel, which is the reverse of going forward.
